scope: Source-derived scheduling/qualification boundary; not a timed cancellation experiment
findings: The pinned nonstreaming _chat checks is_disconnected after a yielded engine event; the bridge consumes normal progress events internally and normally yields only on done or transport timeout. Killing the HTTP client is not a proven timely Native cancellation mechanism.
The pending Queue is not removed by add_aborted_req; a queued cancelled request is consumed later, reset, and skips generate only when its cancelled flag is observed.
An active request checks cancellation between Native input-width8 transactions or decode steps. In-flight CAPI/commit/reset/control work has no proved wall upper bound in this evidence.
The CPU wrapper absolute timeout bounds its own child lifetime, not the remaining Native queue occupancy. Original fixed Slurm/resource deadlines still apply.

Additional actual requests can be separately associated by actual HTTP response ID and Native request_id; the frozen original client count need not equal total Native count. They still compete for the same serial queue.

decision.reason: No demonstrated bound for extra Native occupancy; do not guarantee original-matrix reserve from a CPU timeout. Original491/492/578, stop rules, deadlines, sources and client remain unchanged.
decision.authorization_statement: The earlier separation of a second load from the one-run grant was coordinator scope interpretation, not a new AGENTS/SKILL prohibition or auto-review rejection. No separate second-load authorization or execution was created by this record.
